decision: Separate a new factory-owned execution evaluator from the existing full-graph diagnostic evaluator. Preserve the old diagnostic path and use it to validate the new path. Do not silently delete checks or reuse its graph-proof flags.

current_evidence.scope: 48 independently constructed initial contexts/prefixes and 96 future suffixes, plus diagnostic graphs, comparisons, pins and exports. This is neither an online measurement nor a complete-request 100ms result.
current_evidence.actual_initial_six: Prepared but unexecuted. The 36 focused synthetic tests do not establish native endpoint semantics.

source_call_counts.assumptions: Every one of the 16 groups reaches its first supported known B cut; both suffixes return normally; the first suffix is evaluated before the second. Counts below are source-call accounting, not measured time or proof of cost dominance.
source_call_counts.complete_graph_encodings_for_full32: 272 + sum of the reached prefix collection points across the 16 groups
source_call_counts.inventory_count_scope: One evaluate_declared32 call plus source_proof in each of 32 forks and 32 future resumes. Other source checks are not included.

graph_count_derivation.point_description: One whole graph per reached collection point.

must_remain_in_runtime: Actual exact LocalTransport/session/admission and immutable owned publication history; the own view/own command/received-envelope endpoint evidence and all capture/digest/delivery/current-owner guards.
Actual-origin validation before and after forecasting, and fresh own endpoint collection before returning a local route/transfer proposal. A forecast or saved JSON is never submission authority.

Exactly the fixed Cartesian 32 in original order, 16 independent initial contexts/prefixes and two separately cloned future branches per supported prefix; every failed group retains both unknown candidates.
Original supplied-context construction and all initial/model dynamic guards. This first revision does not cache or remove the 16 initial validations.
Four-frame validation, current popped-event exclusion, world-to-engine and owner-pending aliases, no external recorder, event count/time/horizon semantics and normal activation order.

The unchanged future._cut and fork_later_action/resume_future_later APIs: first known B point only, actual model L identity/generation/traversal, known information, retained ACK/action prefix, strict wire deadline, no earlier consumption and no obsolete action events.
One deepcopy of the complete engine-plus-frame graph for each child, preserving internal aliases; both children are created before either runs. No shared mutable state across model executions.

Complete prediction return and export, exact five finite completion values, empty unknown_information_phases, explicit returned status, complete denominator and strict per-job estimate comparison to an equally computed baseline.
All runtime setup, source checks, guarded contexts, clones, execution, serialization, search, endpoint evidence and failure work remain charged. All methods receive and pay for the same32 provider.
diagnostics_to_keep_in_the_separate_veri: Full engine/frame alias-graph serialization at every cut, fork, sibling check and terminal point.
Complete serialized-graph action-only comparisons and three-graph mutable-id intersections.
Destructive mutation of an already completed child followed by full parent/sibling re-encoding.
Historical target decompression, full prediction byte/type/floathex comparison, expected chronology and native retrospective comparands.
Whole campaign archive and historical-artifact revalidation. This does not excuse actual runtime source identity or accepted-native lifecycle checks.

first_new_implementation.scope: Remove only diagnostic traversals from a private new run_case path, retaining the exact existing future APIs including their repeated source inventories. Do not combine source-proof memoization, context caching, scoped-input optimization, event changes or model export pruning.
first_new_implementation.point_checks: Retain point_description's validate/world/frame/popped-event/no-recorder checks and semantic metadata; omit only the whole-graph encoding/hash fields under a new explicitly named record schema.
first_new_implementation.terminal_checks: Require consumed state and normal returned status; retain terminal counters/time/PC metadata. Do not write a graph equality or destructive-isolation flag that was not computed.
first_new_implementation.ownership_contract: Only exact factory-created engine/frame/branch types, owned by this evaluator invocation, are accepted. Parent and children remain private and no callback receives them. The supplied data is normalized before engine creation; each fork clones the entire dynamic graph once. The audited source closure must exclude custom copy hooks, external mutable handles and reflective mutation. This is a declared closed Python execution domain, not cryptographic capability security or arbitrary in-process tamper resistance.
first_new_implementation.output_contract: A new construction-isolation contract identifies source-derived ownership rather than reusing complete_graph_only_future_action_changed or three_mutable_graphs_disjoint. A corresponding new provider must require returned predictions and this new contract; the frozen provider and old flags stay unchanged.
first_new_implementation.source_equivalence_gate: Use an explicit AST extraction/removal list and inverse reconstruction against the frozen paired run_case. Keep all branch ordering, exception retention, counters, source/current validations and save-before-postchecks ordering. Any statement whose data dependence on removed diagnostics cannot be isolated remains unsupported rather than assumed equivalent.

focused_test_plan: Exact no-restart/four-frame sequence, both children before either resume, immutable earlier three action fields and candidate order32.
Unsupported phase/expired cut/already consumed action/extra collection/obsolete event/changed owner or L identity remains unknown with both siblings retained.
A returned prediction followed by postcondition failure cannot become selectable; save and preserve it with unknown status.
A fake type, unexpected deepcopy hook, shared mutable injected handle, callback access to live state or altered defining global is rejected by the declared factory/source boundary.
Offline graph equality and destructive mutation probes still run in tests/verifier against the new evaluator, independently of its runtime claims.
No diagnostic graph encoder, mutable_ids, action_graph_only or mutate_finished_copy is called by the new runtime; mandatory whole-graph cloning and original dynamic guards still run.

subsequent_fixed_validation_plan.scope: Use the same three frozen initial inputs and all96 action outcomes, never targets as forecast inputs. Compare complete returned prediction bytes/types/floathex/chronology against the already accepted full32 diagnostic evaluator and retain all unknowns. Then use a separately preregistered paired full-cost measurement if correctness closes.
subsequent_fixed_validation_plan.fairness: Every strong method receives the same complete provider/candidate status list, baseline and strict five-job estimate guard. Method index queries are not saved prediction budget. No claim of native joint advantage, hidden-state coverage, or 100ms follows from this change.
subsequent_fixed_validation_plan.future_options_not_in_this_revision: Only after source review and exact output conformance: consider per-invocation source-proof inventory with cheap live function bindings, and immutable initial-fact reuse. Both need separate ownership/lifetime proofs, all setup charged, and no cached native dynamic observations.
